source_item.title: Canadian dollar steadies near 19-month low as oil weakness and rate gap weigh

card.plain_headline: Canadian dollar struggles near 19-month low
card.what_happened: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) is trading near its lowest point in 19 months, weighed down by falling oil prices and a significant interest rate gap between Canada and the United States. This suggests that lower energy prices and higher US interest rates are making the CAD less attractive.
card.what_happened_verbose: The Canadian Dollar has weakened considerably, reaching levels not seen in over a year and a half. Two primary factors are contributing to this decline: a drop in the price of crude oil, a major Canadian export, and a widening difference between interest rates set by the Bank of Canada and the US Federal Reserve. Specifically, if US interest rates are higher or expected to remain higher than Canadian rates, it makes US dollar-denominated assets more attractive to investors, leading to capital outflows from Canada and a weaker CAD.
